scope.rule: Each module is swept against the smallest test-file set that still runs every mutation line of that module. The user ruled on 2026-08-09, and Amendment 3 of #414 records the ruling. The seven modules hold 556 mutations, and the product of the mutation count and the measured cost of each cover is 1.27 hours against a ceiling of four hours.
limits: Every mutation keeps a reader, so a mutation that no case kills is still found. The surviving-mutation signal is preserved.

The cover is conservative in the safe direction. A test file the cover drops might have killed a mutation, so the cover can report a survivor that a wider run would have killed. It over-reports survivors and it does not under-report them.

The candidate set shrinks, because fewer cases are evaluated. The seven sweeps collected 676 cases against the 4411 outcomes of the whole suite. A case the cover drops stays unmeasured against that module, and it is unmeasured and not clean.

tests/test_cli.py runs all 27 reachable mutation lines of ja4plus/output.py on its own, so the cover of that module holds it alone. tests/test_output_schema.py and tests/test_cli_output_option.py hold the larger part of the output cases, and no case of either file is measured against ja4plus/output.py here.

The cover rule drops the lines the import runs, because every test file that imports ja4plus runs them. The rule assumes a mutation line sits inside a function, and 95 of the 279 surviving mutations of these seven modules sit on a line the import runs. ja4plus/__init__.py measures the cost: the cover the rule builds is tests/test_parity.py, and the sweep reads 1 killed and 31 survived. The same 32 mutations against tests/test_public_interface.py, which compares ja4plus.__all__ against a hand-written list, read 25 killed and 7 survived. 24 of the 31 survivors are therefore over-reported, and #433 records the defect in the cover rule.
scope.module_set: The seven Python modules of the top directory of the package. `tests/mutation_sweep.py --module 'ja4plus/*.py'` selects them, because `Path.glob` reads `*` as one path part. **The body of #414 asks a worker to confirm the list against `git ls-files 'ja4plus/*.py'`, and that command names 31 files**, because a git pathspec matches `*` across a directory separator. The instruction is unsatisfiable as written, and this record names the seven files rather than the command. `.claude/rules/conformance.md` already warns about the same reading of `ja4plus/**/*.py`, which names 24.
